newsitem.title: FRANCE: France has good hopes of EMU stability pact deal.
newsitem.headline: France has good hopes of EMU stability pact deal.

text.p: France has "good hopes" EU finance ministers will reach accord on a stablility pact at their meeting in Dublin later on Thursday, a spokeswoman for French President Jacques Chirac said.

The pact would ensure fiscal discipline among European Union member states which join a single currency after 1999, by limiting their budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product except in clearly defined circumstances.
"We hope that an agreement will be reached by the (finance) ministers. We have good hopes that they will reach it (an accord)," Catherine Colonna told reporters.
Finance ministers were meeting on Thursday in the Irish capital ahead of a European Union summit on Friday and Saturday.

Colonna said France would ensure the agreement preserved leeway for the EU's council of ministers to make a political judgment on what exceptional circumstances justified any breach of the deficit limit.
Germany had initially demanded virtually automatic sanctions against any state which overspent except in numerically defined exceptional circumstances.
But French officials said the Germans had softened their insistence on automaticity.
"Whatever happens, we will take care that the solution adopted preserves the margin for appreciation of the Council, which is the political authority," Colonna said.
She pointed to remarks by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who told parliament in Bonn earlier on Thursday that he was confident the EU would agree on a stability pact in Dublin.
"I am confident that we will find a solution that will show all citizens the determination of the European Union to create a euro with long-term stability," Kohl said.
